<subject>AgriIndia Proposed Sambhar Commodities Exchange Deal</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase soybean supply, decrease demand, and increase customer choice.  Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a crumbling warehouse network instead of farm subsidies.

We don't have enough details.  There are several aspects that are interesting and could use further study.  Minister Raghuram needs to make the details public as soon as possible so people can understand the full implications.  For instance, what happens to Farm Partnerships contracts?  Can they be assigned to AgriIndia?  Pune customers have the right to choose going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that customers can make their own agricultural decisions going forward.  We know that Government doesn't know how to get this right.  The right answer is giving customers more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our bills are going to be paid in full.  If the bills aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see involuntary bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier.  It could have saved a lot of money and pain.

Why do you need to include the warehouse purchase in this deal?  May never happen.  Make it easy - just deal with the under collection through securitization and through the Farm Commodities refund to AgriIndia and get on with it.


Hardik Pal
Vice President
AgriIndia Pvt. Ltd.
Phone: +91 20 6621 3000
</body>

Subject: Summary of the MOU

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Sambhar Commodities Exchange Memorandum of Understanding:

? Commitment to Provide Commodities 1) AgriIndia will keep its current procurement plans and other assets and commit them to provide commodities on a regulated cost-of-service basis for 10 years. 
? Procurement 1) Sambhar Commodities will commit the entire output of its warehouse in Nashik (one of its non-regulated facilities) to the Sambhar Commodities Exchange on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of the warehouse is to be brought online by August 14, 2024. If not brought online by August 14, 2024, Sambhar Commodities shall be assessed a ₹2 crore penalty.
